plot: Saturday night in the backyard after apple picking, Mia has burned nine marshmallows at Dad's fire pit and says she'll quit after one more; Pim notices Dad holds his low over the edge but is ignored, Bup's one try to blow out a burning one makes it worse, then fire-shy Crispy steps out of the dark — flames burn, coals cook — and glows his ember eyes over the red coals so Mia holds her last marshmallow there; it turns perfect gold, Zeek climbs on the cracker to measure it and gets squished into a s'more, and June calls over the fence that someone just bought the old bakery.

script.title: Mia Burned 9 Marshmallows in a Row

beats.say: Fire! Mia's marshmallow is on fire again! Run, everybody!
F-f-fire? Nope! Beans and fire do not mix!
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Saturday night, in the backyard. The family is back from apple picking.
And yes. Lolly went too, riding in Mia's jacket pocket.
I picked an apple. Well, I sat on one. Same thing.
Now Dad has lit the little fire pit. It's s'mores night.
Dad's marshmallow comes out golden brown. Every single time.
Mia's go black. Nine of them. Crunchy, smoky, ruined.
W-wait. Dad holds his low, by the edge. Not the middle.
Irrelevant, Pim. My calculations say it is the stick.
Far away, in the dark grass, Crispy hasn't moved one inch.
I don't do fire. Fire did me. Long ago.
Then Mia drops her stick and sits down on the grass.
I'm just bad at marshmallows, she says. One more. Then I quit.
One left. If it burns, Mia quits forever. Not tonight.
Okay team, here's the move. When it catches, I blow it out.
Bup, you are bread. Your lungs are mostly holes.
Mia pushes the last marshmallow right into the tall yellow flames.
Bup jumps up on the stones and blows. Hard. Fffffff!
The flame on the marshmallow only grows bigger.
A burning blob drips off and lands right next to Pim.
Th-that's it. I'm moving to the freezer. Goodbye forever.
Mia blows the flame out herself. It's only half black. She sighs.
She's got one more try before Mom calls everyone in. That's it.
Last chance, team. If this one burns, Mia never tries again.
Then somebody say something smart. Anybody. Please.
And out of the dark grass, slowly, comes Crispy.
The flames don't cook anything. They just burn. I know.
The coals cook. Low. Red. Quiet. Pim said it first.
I did? By the edge! Over the red bits! I said that!
Correction. The stick was fine. The bean was right. Again.
But how do we tell Mia where to hold it?
Easy. I glow. She'll follow the glow.
Crispy walks to the very edge of the pit. Into the heat.
His ember eyes light up, bright orange, above the quiet coals.
Mia looks up. Huh. A glowing little rock. Right there, she whispers.
She holds the last marshmallow low, just over Crispy's glow.
Don't. Rush. Turn it slowly. Like a sunset.
One minute. It puffs up. It turns golden. Not one black spot.
Mia jumps so high her hat falls off. I did it!
Team, we did it. Well, Crispy did. Okay, Pim did. Fine.
Zeek climbs onto the cracker to measure that perfect golden color.
My calculations say this is the best marshmallow in history.
Mia drops the marshmallow on the cracker. Right on top of Zeek.
Then she presses the second cracker down. Squish.
I'm sticky. I'm warm. I am a dessert. This was not calculated.
Mia laughs so hard she lets him slide out, gooey and grinning.
Welcome to the burnt club, genius. It's warm here.
Then, over the fence, a voice. It's June, the neighbor.
The old bakery on our street, she calls. Somebody bought it today.
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
